data.name: Shiva
data.gender_notes: Shiva is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who destroys the ignorance and negativity in the world and helps in the creation and preservation of the universe. The name Shiva carries the meaning “The Destroyer” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shiva usually hope their child will grow to embody the destroyer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the ultimate reality and represents the divine force of destruction and transformation.
data.etymology: Shiva belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Destroyer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shiva total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Shiva is a central figure in Hinduism, known as the Destructor or the Transformer. He is represented as a third-eye icon, a symbol of wisdom and knowledge. Shiva is also known as the Lord of Dance, and his dance is believed to create the rhythm of the universe. In Indian art, Shiva's image is often depicted in various forms such as Ardhanarishvara (half-male, half-female), Nataraja (Lord of Dance), and Lingam (phallic symbol of Shiva). These images are deeply ingrained in Indian culture and are found in various temples and monuments across India and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: Shiva represents the destructive aspect of God, which is necessary for the cycle of creation, preservation, and destruction. He is also known as the God of Transformation, symbolizing the ability to change and grow. In Hinduism, the ultimate goal is to attain moksha, or liberation from the cycle of birth and death. Shiva is believed to be the gateway to this spiritual journey, helping his devotees to purify their minds and overcome ignorance and negativity. Shiva is also often regarded as the Supreme Reality or the Ultimate Consciousness in Hindu philosophy. Thus, Shiva is not only a destructive force but also a source of spiritual transformation and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shiva represents the supreme cosmic power, the destroyer and the transformer. He is the embodiment of destruction and creation, symbolizing the cyclic nature of the universe.

vedic_reference.note: Shiva is one of the primary deities in Hinduism and is also known as Mahadeva, Mahasena, and Pashupati.

historical_references.reference: Shiva was one of the primary deities of the early Hindu civilization in the Indus Valley Civilization around 3300-1900 BCE.
historical_references.context: The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was an ancient civilization in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent. It is characterized by urban settlements (many with bastions), a complex system of drainage, and a well-planned urban structure.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Shiva emerged as a major deity in Hinduism during the Shiva Purana period, around 500-1200 CE. The name Shiva carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Shiva Purana is one of the eighteen major Puranas, ancient Hindu texts that focus on the stories of various Hindu deities. It is believed to have been compiled around the 12th century CE, but the actual texts may be much older. The text describes Shiva as the destroyer of evil and the god of regeneration and creation.

modern_usage.modern_context: Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction and regeneration, is a popular cultural figure with a modern following. His symbolism of transformation, detachment, and spiritual growth resonates with contemporary trends. On Instagram, users post images of Shiva statues, temples, and related artwork using the #shiva and #hinduism hashtags. On Facebook, communities exist for sharing devotional practices and knowledge about Shiva's stories and rituals. Twitter is filled with inspirational quotes and thoughts about Shiva, often shared with the #ShivaQuotes hashtag. Overall, Shiva's modern context is intertwined with spirituality, yoga, meditation, fitness, and self-improvement.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Devi Shiva in Kathmandu, Nepal attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Shiva, which means "The Destroyer". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
